title: The Macro-Fiscal-Energy Scenario Tool
subtitle: Linking energy investment and carbon pricing to growth, revenue and debt in one workbook
message: One workbook for 186 countries chains investment needs, a carbon-pricing feasibility screen, open lite versions of three IMF and World Bank macro models and a debt test. Financing and efficiency move the result more than the size of the program.

problem.title: Four teams, four numbers that do not add up

stats.label: of GDP: Kenya's net zero budget need in 2030
of GDP added to Kenya's public debt by 2050

problem.text: The investment need, the carbon-tax revenue, the growth effect and the debt test are usually run by different teams on different calibrations. The tool runs them in one pass, with every assumption a visible cell.

mechanism.title: Financing and efficiency matter most
mechanism.caption: GIMF-lite, stylized program of 1% of GDP a year for ten years.
points: Earmarked carbon revenue cuts the debt peak by 4 points.
Lower efficiency cuts the GDP gain by 30–40% at the same debt.
Kenya: pricing covers about 5% of the need; a clean grid leaves little to tax.

action.title: Compare packages, not countries
results: Kenya is at high debt risk before the program and after it.
The two macro families differ most on energy savings and private investment.
Lite models do not replace their parents.
